The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13-06-2023.

sentences.text:
The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 13-06-2023 at about 11.45 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in TVS XL bearing No. KA.52.U.0330 on Nelamangala - Bengaluru BH road, when they reached near Durga Grand hotel, Nelamangala town, Bangalore rural district, at that time, driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital,
Nelamangala, wherein first aid treatment was taken and then shifted to Victoria hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.

The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance and nourishment charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and was doing coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending tractor are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of summons, both the respondents have appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed separate written statement.

Respondent No.1 - insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the issuance of policy to the offending tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 by contending that, this respondent has issued the policy to the tractor from 28-01-2022 to 27-01-2023, but accident was occurred on 13-06-2023 and further it has issued the policy from 08-07-2023 to 07-07-2024.
Hence as on the date of accident the policy was not in force.

Further it has denied the avocation and income of the petitioner and also the injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident,
treatment taken and amount spent towards medical expenses.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, arbitrary, baseless and speculative.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. Respondent No.2 - owner has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also the injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident, treatment taken and amount spent towards medical expenses.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the involvement of the offending tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 in the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, arbitrary, baseless and speculative.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

5. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

2 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 by its driver, in RTA took place on 13-06-2023 at about 11.45 p.m., on Nelamangala - Ben- galuru BH road, infront of Durga Grand hotel, Nelamangala town, Ban- galore Rural District ?
2. Whether the petitioner is enti- tled for compensation?

If so, at what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Further the Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopaedic surgeon at Victoria hospital is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P12 to P14.
On the other hand, 1st respondent insurance company has examined its official as RW.1 and Ex.R1 to R6 were got marked.
Further the driver of the tractor is examined as RW.2 and Ex.R7 is got marked.

7. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
8.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;

 ISSUE NO.1 :
9.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of her case, she has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
10.

On perusal of Ex.P1 - FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Shettallaiah, who is the rider of the TVS XL motor cycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of tractor bearing No.
KA.52.T.1231.
The contents of Ex.P.1 & 2 are in consonance with the petition averments.

3 registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the IO has conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.

sentences.text: On perusal of contents of Ex.P3, the accident spot is near the northern divider edge.

Further the Ex.P4 being the IMV report shows that the motor cycle bearing No. KA.52.U.0330 has got damages in its crash guard right side and center stand, but the offending tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 has not got any damages.
11. The respondent No.2 owner of the offending Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 examined the driver of said offending tractor as RW.2.
On perusal of the evidence of RW.2 the fact of accident is admitted but they have denied their part of negligence.
Even though the RW.2 deposed by denying his negligence, as admitted by the RW.2 the charge sheet is filed against him after the investigation.
Except the oral evidence of RW.2 no evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 owner to deny the case of the petitioner.

Thus, the contents of Ex.P3 mahazar along with the contents of Ex.P4 IMV report supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligence driving by the driver of tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231.
12.

Ex.P6 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the offending tractor bearing No.
KA.52.T.1231 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC, wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231.
It is very important to note that the said charge sheet is not challenged by the respondent No.2 owner or its driver to substantiate their defence.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence on the part of petitioner also.

13. The respondent No.1- insurance company has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability and examined its official as RW.1 but the evidence of RW.1 in respect of fact of negligence cannot be accepted as he is not an eye witness and his evidence is based on the documents whereas the documents speaks about the negligence of the driver of Tractor bearing No.
KA.52.T.1231.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231.
14.
The charge sheet is came to be filed against the driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231.

Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

sentences.text: In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 13-06-2023 which is caused by the driver of tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 which belonging to respondent No.2.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that she has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of respondent No.2.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 39 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P8 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 01-01-1984, the accident was occurred on 13-06-2023, Hence as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 39 years.
In the petition itself she has averred that immediately after the accident she was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7 the petitioner was inpatient from 13-06-2023 to 19-06-2023 and has sustained right sided type 3b open shaft of BB leg fracture and also underwent operation of CRIF with ILN tibia.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.85,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P10 amounting Rs.8,714/-
which are supported by medical prescriptions as per Ex.P11 and Ex.P6 charge sheet.
No grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off Sushilamma vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155354204/
5 the same i.e., Rs.9,000/-.

sentences.text: c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident she was doing coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
In this regard petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.7 the petitioner was admitted to Victoria hospital for a period of 7 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period including 7 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000 /- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by her the petitioner has examined Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria as PW.2 and through him clinical notes, inpatient case details and X- rays were got marked at Ex.P12 to 14.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained right sided type III B Open shaft of both bones leg fracture and also underwent operation for CRIF with ILN of tibia.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered the disability of right lower limb at 36% and whole body disability at 18%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner she was doing coolie work.

The alleged injuries and the evidence of the PW.2 doctor reveals that the petitioner complains of pain in right knee, difficulty to squat on floor,
sit cross legged, climb up stairs, walk on slope, kneel and stand on affected limb.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on her occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 14% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '15'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 15 X 14% = Rs.4,03,200/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P7 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 7 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the petitioner has sustained simple as well as grievous injuries.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period she spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained she is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 7 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.7,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 7 days in the hospital.

6 g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:

sentences.text: The petitioner admitted to the hospitals for the injuries sustained by her, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.35,000/- under this head.
h) Future medical expenses:
The PW.2 in his evidence affidavit has stated that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implant which costs around Rs.12,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.10,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 85,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs. 9,000/- c.
Towards loss of income during Rs. 64,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 4,03,200/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 25,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 7,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 35,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 10,000/-

LIABILITY:
20.

As per the reasons discussed in Issue No.1 the petitioner has got injuries in the RTA dated 13-06-2023 which was caused by the actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 and the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
21.
The present petition is filed U/Sec.166 of IMV Act by claiming the compensation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are the insurer and owner of the tractor.
The respondent No.2 is the insurer of the Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231.
At the cost of repetition as per the reasons discussed in Issue No.1 the negligence of the driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 is established.
When the petition filed U/Sec.166 of IMV Act by claiming the compensation the fact of negligence place very important role to fix the liability.

In this regard the petitioner successfully established the negligence of the driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231.
22.
It is contended by the petitioner that as on the date of accident ie., on 13-06-2023 the offending Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 was duly insured with the respondent No.1 insurance company.

But the said fact is specifically denied by the respondent No.1 insurance company by stating that there was no policy was issued which was Sushilamma vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155354204/
7 valid as on the date of accident and they have issued the policy to the offending Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 by contending that, this respondent No.1 insurance company has issued the policy to the tractor from 28-01-2022 to 27-01-2023, but accident was occurred on 13-06-2023 and further it has issued the policy from 08-07-2023 to 07-07-2024.

sentences.text: The Ex.P6 charge sheet also reveals that the Sec.196 of IMV Act was invoked against the driver of Tractor bearing No. KA.52.T.1231 for driving the uninsured tractor in the public road.
The evidence of RW.1 coupled with the documents produced by the petitioner successfully establishes that there was no insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Hence in the absence of policy the respondent No.2 owner has to pay the compensation along with interest @
6% p.a.

Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative ISSUE NO.3:
23.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petition against the respondent No.1 - insurance company stands dismissed.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,38,200/- (Rupees Six lakhs thirty eight thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition.
The respondent No.2 - owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

h) Future medical expenses:
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.10,000/- under this head.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 85,000/- b.
Towards medical expenses Rs. 9,000/- c.
Towards loss of income during Rs. 64,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 4,03,200/- e.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 7,000/- g.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 10,000/-
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petition against the respondent No.1 - insurance company stands dismissed.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,38,200/- (Rupees Six lakhs thirty eight thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition.
The respondent No.2 - owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
